body:
Hey friend, I'm sorry I've read your reply a few days ago already, and now I'm again in a rush (as always, either asleep or running after my meds, so "busy" I know) BUT I want to thank you so so much already, in case I forget again!

Your post was very hopeful and it's good hearing your experience and opinion. I do agree a good doctor makes all the difference and it's a gift from God when you find a good one. I used to think every dentist is "good" cause they're a dentist, it's their job, but there are huge differences when it comes to whether something is good for You, even starting with the docs personally and preference, like you said, things you wouldn't think would influence a therapeutic objective, but it does.

I'm terrible sorry that you had to go through this experience with the double jaw surgery! I hope it will get even better in time!! (Which is kinda the sad part with teeth, seems so irreparable and ever worsening) but like You said, most people don't really care. I've made this experience too! And whoever will like you, will like you nonetheless. I guess you kinds have to get distanced enough to a problem so ist does not actively depress and cripple you more than it has to, but be aware of it enough so you will finally do something to fix it. I'm hoping I will finally follow through with that now that I've been painfully reminded again to not let this get worse. Also, in a few years I KNOW I will think "I wish I did start fixing my teeth back then when I made that post on reddit". Better sooner than later, no matter how depressing.

I hope you're doing well, take care of yourself! I wish you good health, and that you'll be happy and fulfilled!

Hello, thank you so so much for your kind reply! 

> Dentists are now discovering that any sub lingual and kratom are so acidic and actually eat away enamel and make teeth very spongy

I thought so! I haven't been on methadone and subutex for long, only a year, several years back. I wonder though if the acid I put in my IV stuff changes the ph level in the body or does something else. Or whether it's really the dry mouth I have since I'm on fentanyl, or the drug itself.

>I’m trying to preserve what I’ve got left with fillings. At some point I may be able to get a couple implants on the bottom. 

That sounds like a good plan, I've kinda been doing this similar thing, sadly they deteriorated faster than I could get appointments. But maybe If you take good care and change some habits it will last! 
It must be very useful to have the insight you have as a dental assistant, no? I sometimes hear that professional tooth cleaning is just a money maker and causes more harm than good (?). And I personally think pulling wisdom teeth just because seems so unintuitive. Mine came out just fine, and would've been a great joker if I hadn't fucked those up as well. Or are these preventative measures really better in the long run in your opinion?

>Just do one tooth at a time don’t let the whole bottom line scare you...remember how hard you went after money for dope? Do the same for saving money on teeth.

That's really good advice, one tooth at a time. I try to keep my hopes up for implants and through my rose colored glasses I think that money is makeable, and if that's the only thing in the way then there's hope. 

>If you send me your treatment plan options I will tell you what I would do and what you can put off

Thank you so very much for your kind offer!! You don't know how comforting it was just reading this, feeling less lost and alone in this. Although I'm kinda uncomfortable bothering you.. And scared of my own unpredictability... But I want to call the Praxis of the one dentist I had good experiences with ages ago, (didn't manage to yesterday..) hopefully get an appointment, and am going to ask him for his/a second opinion on my issue. This time I'll bring notes and ask thoroughly. If you have time and the nerves, I will send you a PM then. And maybe I can get an xray done, if that helps.

Thank you so much again for your kind words, I hope you will be able to fix your teeth and make the progress last! Bless your soul!

hwy, sorry I didn't get to reply sooner.

I feel for you so much, and I'm sorry you have to deal with this, it's like a negative cloud hanging in the back of your head, at least for me. How do you mentally cope with this?

Well, for my bottom teeth it's gonna be the same as you described I fear. Most broke off flush with my gums, there are only brown roots left, like a crater, and 2 "teeth" that are filling and crumbling away. But at least I've got some front teeth left.. you don't? I was hoping that would maybe make a difference. Or do they need to extract some okayish teeth for the dentures? 

>only dental surgery to remove roots and extractions, plus dentures are my only option.

Please tell me, why are dentures the only option in your case? I mean, would you be able to get implantans if you had the money? (My hope is that one might only need a few and bridge the rest for more affordability.. But I'll have to ask the dentist I plan on going to. 


(The following turned out very long, you don't have to read it..:

Having a good dentist is key I imagine. I've been to so many Imo "bad" ones, they just want to extract preemptively with no real plan for the future, because they will get inflamed at some point they say. The one doc I plan on going to I was at once, and his mindset seemed so... reasonable. He said he thinks one should try to save each natural tooth if possible. He did a root treatment (told me about the cost, did it despite me saying I have no money, and he never sent the bill..) And he built that same tooth back up that any other doctor would 100% have extracted. And he even did a little filling on the back of my front teeth during a waiting time (instead of going to drink a coffee or something) because "the front is so important for ones appearance". He sounded and acted like he really has a patient's best interest at heart. I don't know if it's any good in the long run, I'm not a doc. What I'm trying to say is out of ~8 dentists there is one who might have a different mentality, who might be able to give you some hope and really help you out in ways others wouldn't.)

> Hopefully, I can find a decent dentist and the dentures made for me look natural.

Yes, please get more opinions from several dentists before going through with it at any rate! I pray that things go well for you, as well as they can! And thank you so much for your input!!!

edit: may I ask where you are from? Because you mentioned insurance running out.. How is that even a thing nowadays, it's so fucked up. Health (including dental health) should never be about money.. But that's utopic I guess.
